items.text: A full understanding of how cis-platin kills cancer cells is beyond the aims of this book.Put simply:

items.label: list_item
items.text: ·All cells, including cancer cells, contain deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA).

items.label: list_item
items.text: The structure of cis-platin enables it to form a bond between the two strands of DNA (fig C), which prevents them from separating and so prevents the cancer cells from dividing.

items.label: caption
items.text: fig CDNA strands are shown in grey and cis-platin in pink.

items.label: text
items.text: The isomers trans-platin and cis-platin have different structures. The difference in structure means that trans-platin is a much less effective cancer treatment than cis-platin.It is also more toxic. So, it is important touseonly thecis-isomer in thecancertreatment.
